account:
Today I have kept my office, mill inspection, lunch and council-letter appointments, though I reached the office late. Something unusual seems to centre on the bakery. Several townsfolk independently repeated talk of a 'bridge or port change' there, but none has explained what actually changed. Reports name the baker and neighbour as present and mention the baker carrying a sack of bread. I have not witnessed any bridge or port work myself, so I cannot yet tell whether this is real infrastructure business or garbled gossip.

There is clearly substantial bread business underway. The secretary's report records freight arranging an order of 200 loaves: the baker acknowledged 24 emeralds and 72 wheat, with another 528 wheat needed and hauling still to be arranged. Earlier today I overheard the baker saying the bakery chest was empty and seeking a bread settlement and thirty emeralds promised by the innkeeper. These may be related transactions, but I do not know that. The baker has just shouted somewhere beyond intelligible hearing.

At the mill we confirmed seventy-three hay bales at two emeralds each, but neither supplier commitments nor delivery terms. No town purchase has been authorized. The secretary has been helping investigate and keeping reports, yet I have not actually received any council letters today; I have just asked whether any arrived. Tea with the neighbour is scheduled for three, and the builder's great-hall lighting inspection for six was explicitly authorized by me yesterday. Those appointments could offer chances to learn more, but I have no evidence that they conceal another purpose. My best current guess is that bread supply, payments and transport arrangements are proceeding among freight, baker and perhaps innkeeper and neighbour without my understanding the full plan. I need direct explanations rather than treating repeated rumours as established facts.
